findings.title: Controlled painting collection
findings.conclusion: The evaluation covers a balanced 50-painting collection with ten paintings in each of five visual categories.
findings.plain_implication: The balanced collection supports controlled within-benchmark comparisons, but conclusions must remain limited to this collection.
findings.limitation: The controlled collection does not establish real-world conservation generality.

findings.title: Approved restoration evidence
findings.conclusion: All 1,785 approved candidates remain available for filtering and case-level inspection.
findings.plain_implication: The complete candidate catalog remains available for inspection; the report does not rely only on its selected examples.
findings.limitation: Candidate count is not an independent sample-size claim because repeated seeds and models share cases.

findings.title: Strongest general benchmark result
findings.conclusion: LaMa ranks first on 10 of 11 quality anchors. Within this controlled benchmark, it is the strongest general restoration baseline across error, colour, perceptual, feature, seam, texture, and structural-affinity evidence.
findings.plain_implication: LaMa is the best default baseline among the three fully evaluated methods when several forms of evidence are considered together.
findings.scope: three fully evaluated models across 410 cases
findings.limitation: Anchor wins are metric-specific benchmark results, not conservation approval or historical authenticity.

findings.title: One metric changes the winner
findings.conclusion: OpenCV Telea narrowly leads crop SSIM, while LaMa leads the other ten anchors. SSIM alone would therefore give an incomplete account of restoration quality.
findings.plain_implication: A conclusion based only on SSIM would favour Telea and conceal LaMa's broader advantage. Metric choice materially changes the verdict.
findings.limitation: The result demonstrates metric disagreement; it does not make either model universally correct.

findings.title: Repeated-run uncertainty coverage
findings.conclusion: Repeated-seed evidence covers 130 canonical groups and 35 damage-size groups for Stable Diffusion.
findings.plain_implication: Stable Diffusion outputs that change more across seeds should receive closer visual inspection.
findings.limitation: Seed variability is an empirical uncertainty proxy, not calibrated confidence.

findings.title: SDXL remains bounded evidence
findings.conclusion: SDXL contributes ten completed cases for qualitative and bounded comparison, not a fourth full benchmark.
findings.plain_implication: SDXL can be discussed as a feasibility result, but it cannot be ranked as a fully evaluated fourth model.
findings.limitation: SDXL results must not be generalized to all 410 restoration-eligible cases.

findings.title: Human review remains central
findings.conclusion: 1,703 of 1,785 candidates trigger conservative review guidance. Automated restoration should support inspection, not replace expert judgement.
findings.plain_implication: The conservative flag rate makes automated restoration unsuitable for unsupervised acceptance.
findings.limitation: Computational review flags are diagnostic rules, not expert annotations or conservation ground truth.

findings.title: No universal restoration score
findings.conclusion: The evaluation keeps metric families, regions, uncertainty, and failure evidence separate so that important disagreements remain visible.
findings.plain_implication: Keeping evidence separate prevents a convenient single number from hiding metric and regional disagreement.
findings.limitation: The dashboard supports evidence review and does not produce conservation approval.
